Claude Opus 5 vs Fable 5: Which Should You Actually Use in 2026?

Update, September 2026: Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.1 on September 1, 2026. Base pricing didn't change (still $10/$50 per million tokens), so the price comparison below still holds against Fable 5.1. What did change: Fable 5.1 improved on several benchmarks this piece cites for Fable 5, including CursorBench 3.2.0 (70.5% to 73.4%) and OSWorld 2.0 partial (72.9% to 77.9%), and cache read pricing dropped 75%. More notably, Anthropic's own guidance has shifted since this was written: the company now recommends Opus 5 as the default pick for most workloads over the Fable line, reinforcing rather than reversing this page's verdict. See what changed in Fable 5.1 for the full breakdown before assuming any specific benchmark number below still applies exactly to Fable 5.1.

Anthropic just shipped a model that ranks above Fable 5 on the industry's main intelligence leaderboard and costs half as much per token. That is not a marketing claim, it is what Artificial Analysis measured the day Opus 5 launched.

Claude Opus 5 went live on July 24, 2026, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, exactly half of Fable 5's $10/$50. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Opus 5 scores 61, Fable 5 scores 60, and GPT-5.6 Sol scores 59. For the first time since Fable 5 launched, there is a model that is priced like the budget option and benchmarks like the flagship.

This is a genuine head-to-head, not a hypothetical one. Fable 5 spent three weeks offline after a June 12, 2026 export-control directive, and Anthropic restored it globally on July 1 with a new safety classifier. Both models are live right now, which means the choice between them is no longer forced. It comes down to what you are actually building.
Here is the honest comparison: intelligence, price, coding, computer use and agent tasks, where each model actually wins, and which one to put in production today.
What is Claude Opus 5?

Opus 5 (model id claude-opus-5) is Anthropic's new flagship reasoning and coding model, announced July 24, 2026. It replaces Opus 4.8 as Anthropic's top-tier offering and is priced identically to how Opus 4.8 was priced: $5 per million input tokens, $25 per million output tokens.

The pitch from Anthropic and confirmed independently by Artificial Analysis is straightforward: near-Fable-5 intelligence, at half of Fable 5's cost, with a clear edge on computer-use and automation benchmarks. That combination is the actual story here. Most model releases bump one number and leave price untouched.

How does Opus 5 compare on intelligence benchmarks?

The cleanest single number for comparing frontier models right now is the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an aggregate score across a battery of independent benchmarks, run the same way for every model on the leaderboard.
Opus 5 (max configuration) landed at 61, the top score of the 170 models Artificial Analysis tracks. Fable 5 sits at 60. GPT-5.6 Sol sits at 59. The gap between first and third place is one point.

That one-point gap is why "near-Fable-5 intelligence" is the accurate framing rather than "better than Fable 5 across the board." Opus 5 edges out Fable 5 on this aggregate score, but the two models are close enough that the real differentiator is not the index number, it is which specific tasks you run.

Where does Opus 5 actually beat Fable 5?
Anthropic's own launch benchmarks, run against Fable 5 and Opus 4.8, point to a handful of tasks where Opus 5 is the clear leader:
Frontier-Bench: Opus 5 surpasses all models tested, more than doubling Opus 4.8's score. This is the largest jump of any benchmark in the release.
ARC-AGI 3: Opus 5 scores roughly 3x the next-best model, the single biggest margin in the announcement.
OSWorld 2.0 (computer-use tasks: operating a real desktop, clicking through real applications): Opus 5 beats Fable 5 while running at roughly one third of Fable 5's cost for the same task.
Zapier AutomationBench (workflow automation tasks): Opus 5 scores about 1.5x the next-best model.

The pattern across all four is consistent: Opus 5's biggest wins are in agentic and computer-use tasks, the categories that matter most if you are actually deploying models to run workflows rather than just answer questions in a chat window.
Where is Opus 5 close, or behind?
Two honest caveats belong in this comparison, because a fair vs post reports the losses too.

CursorBench 3.2 (real-world coding assistance): Opus 5 lands within 0.5% of Fable 5, at half the cost. That is not a win for Opus 5, it is a tie on quality with a clear win on price. If your workload is day-to-day coding assistance rather than long autonomous agent runs, that near-tie is the number to anchor on.

Cybersecurity benchmarks: Opus 5 trails Mythos 5, Anthropic's other frontier model, on cybersecurity-specific tasks. Mythos 5 remains restricted to a smaller set of vetted US organizations even after Fable 5's global restoration, so this is not a like-for-like Fable 5 comparison, but it is the one category where Opus 5 is not the best Anthropic has shipped.

Put together: Opus 5 is not "better than Fable 5 at everything." It is priced at half of Fable 5, ties or beats it on the benchmarks that matter for most production workloads, and clearly wins on the automation and computer-use tasks that decide whether an AI agent can actually finish a job unsupervised.

Is Fable 5 even available right now?

Yes, as of this writing. Fable 5 was suspended for roughly three weeks after a June 12, 2026 export-control directive, then restored globally on July 1, 2026, after the Commerce Department lifted the controls and Anthropic added a new safety classifier targeting the jailbreak technique that triggered the order. Mythos 5 came back more narrowly, limited to a smaller set of vetted US organizations rather than a full global restore.

That history still matters for this comparison. If you migrated off Fable 5 during the suspension using an alternative, our Claude Fable 5 alternatives guide covers what teams switched to at the time, and Opus 5 is now the strongest reason not to switch back: it closes most of the intelligence gap to Fable 5 while keeping Opus 4.8's lower price. FAQ
What is Claude Opus 5?

Claude Opus 5 (model id claude-opus-5) is Anthropic's flagship model, launched July 24, 2026, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens. It replaces Opus 4.8 as Anthropic's top-tier model and scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, the highest of any model on that leaderboard.
Is Claude Opus 5 better than Fable 5?

Opus 5 scores one point higher than Fable 5 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (61 vs 60) and costs half as much per token. It clearly leads on computer-use and automation benchmarks like OSWorld 2.0 and Zapier AutomationBench, while landing within 0.5% of Fable 5 on coding benchmarks like CursorBench 3.2. It is not better at everything, but it beats or ties Fable 5 on the benchmarks that matter most for production agent work, at half the price.
How much does Claude Opus 5 cost compared to Fable 5?

Opus 5 costs $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens. Fable 5 costs $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. Opus 5 is priced at exactly half of Fable 5 across both input and output tokens.
Is Claude Fable 5 available right now?

Yes. Fable 5 was suspended for about three weeks after a June 12, 2026 export-control directive, then restored globally on July 1, 2026, once the Commerce Department lifted the controls and Anthropic added a new safety classifier. Mythos 5 came back only for a smaller set of vetted US organizations, not a full global restore.
Does Opus 5 beat Fable 5 on coding?

Not by much. On CursorBench 3.2, a real-world coding assistance benchmark, Opus 5 lands within 0.5% of Fable 5's score, at half the cost. For coding-specific workloads, treat the two models as roughly tied on quality, with Opus 5 winning clearly on price.
What is Opus 5's biggest weakness?

Cybersecurity-specific benchmarks. Opus 5 trails Mythos 5, Anthropic's other frontier model, on cybersecurity tasks specifically. It is not a weakness relative to Fable 5, since Fable 5's cybersecurity performance was not specified in Anthropic's own benchmarks, but it is the one category where Opus 5 is not Anthropic's strongest model.
Should I migrate from Opus 4.8 to Opus 5?

If you were already running Opus 4.8, Opus 5 is a same-price upgrade: identical $5/$25 per million token pricing, with a meaningfully higher Intelligence Index score and a large jump on Frontier-Bench, described by Anthropic as more than doubling Opus 4.8's score. There is no cost penalty for making the switch, which makes it one of the easier model upgrades to justify.
